item.title: Transkittenism vs necrocracy vs radical xenophobia
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Transkittenism, Necrocracy, and Radical Xenophobia are mutually exclusive late-game policies available after you have traded with the Leviathans. You can only pick one per run, and they cannot be changed once selected.

Because they are exclusive, choosing one requires identifying your primary bottleneck: storage capacity, raw production, or specific resource pacts.

Comparison Overview

Policy Primary Focus Key Benefit
Transkittenism Storage Increases Moon Base storage capacity (which effectively allows for more Chronospheres).
Necrocracy Production Global production bonus based on your Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) levels.
Radical Xenophobia Diplomacy/Pacts Increases Mausoleum efficiency and grants 5 free Pacts.

Deep Dive

1. Transkittenism (The “Storage” Choice)

  • Best for: Players aiming for “Chronosphere amplification” or pushing to reach higher kitten counts through storage-based building limits.
  • The Effect: It doubles Gigaflop output. Because Gigaflops are used to maintain Entanglement Stations (which boost relic output) and affect Moon Base storage, it helps you manage higher building caps.
  • Why pick it: If you are planning a very long run where you want to maximize the number of Chronospheres you can build, the extra storage from Moon Bases provided by Transkittenism is often the superior choice.

2. Necrocracy (The “Production” Choice)

  • Best for: Players who have significant Black Liquid Sorrow (BLS) and want to maximize Unobtainium, ivory, and alicorn production.
  • The Effect: Provides a global production bonus of 0.1% per 1% of BLS. It also boosts your Leviathan Energy Cap by 5%.
  • Why pick it: If your main limitation is the speed at which you generate resources (Unobtainium being the most common), Necrocracy is mathematically superior in the late game. As your BLS increases over multiple runs, this bonus scales significantly, potentially tripling your Unobtainium production.

3. Radical Xenophobia (The “Niche” Choice)

  • Best for: Very specific scenarios where you need Pacts or want to maximize the efficacy of your Mausoleums.
  • The Effect: Increases the efficacy of all Mausoleums and gives 5 free Pacts.
  • Why pick it: This is generally considered the weakest of the three for most standard gameplay goals. It is mostly used if you specifically need the Pacts for a challenge or a very unconventional setup.

Strategic Recommendation

  • Early/Mid-Late Game: If you don’t have much BLS built up yet, Transkittenism is often preferred for the storage flexibility.
  • Deep/Infinite Runs: Once you have high levels of BLS (usually 250+), Necrocracy typically outperforms Transkittenism by providing a massive, multiplicative production boost to your entire economy, including space structures.
  • Note on AI Apocalypse: Be aware that Necrocracy can make managing the AI Apocalypse more complex because it increases your reliance on the resources that trigger it. If you want to avoid the headache of managing AI cores vs. Entanglement stations, some players stick with Transkittenism purely for the “lazier” late-game management.

Summary: If you aren’t sure, Transkittenism is generally safer and more flexible for storage, while Necrocracy is the “power gamer” move for when your production speed (specifically Unobtainium) becomes your primary blocker.

item.title: Outer Space Treaty vs Military Space
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Outer Space Treaty and Militarize Space are mutually exclusive Foreign policies that become available after you launch your first Satellite. Both cost 10,000 Culture to unlock, and picking one will permanently lock you out of the other for the rest of your run.

Here is a comparison of their effects and the community’s strategic advice on when to choose them:

Outer Space Treaty

  • The Effect: This policy establishes that space is the domain of all races, which improves your standing with all trading partners. The boost is equivalent to having 10 extra Tradeposts.
  • When to choose it: Community guides generally recommend picking Outer Space Treaty for most standard situations. Trade is a fundamental pillar of the mid-to-late game economy, making the diplomatic relations boost consistently useful.

Militarize Space

  • The Effect: This policy turns your satellites into military research hubs. It makes the maximum science capacity bonus that your Satellites provide to your Observatories 10% more powerful.
  • When to choose it: You should pick Militarize Space specifically if you find that your progression is constantly being blocked by your maximum science limit. The extra capacity boost can help you afford expensive space structures and technologies when your science storage is bottlenecked.

Strategic Value

Given that you are managing Enriched Uranium and Distortion, Knowledge Sharing is a fundamental building block you likely acquired to scale your Science cap. Here is why it remains relevant in the late game:

  1. Reaching the Antimatter Era: To unlock Antimatter and Relic-based technologies, you need Science caps in the millions. Knowledge Sharing acts as a multiplier that makes every Library, Academy, and BioLab more potent.
  2. Reset Efficiency: When you reset (especially with Chronospheres), Knowledge Sharing is one of the early upgrades you want to grab to quickly regain your tech tree progress.
  3. Leader Synergy: If your Leader is a Scientist, the Knowledge Sharing bonus stacks with the Leader’s rank bonus, allowing for massive bursts of Science generation.

Pro Tip: If you find yourself “Science-capped” (unable to afford the next tech even when your storage is full), focus on building more BioLabs and Compendiums. Knowledge Sharing will then apply its percentage bonus to that higher base.

item.title: Immortalism
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Immortalism is a high-level Metaphysics upgrade that fundamentally changes how your kittens interact with the cycle of life and death—specifically concerning their rank and experience.

Key Effects

The primary function of Immortalism is to preserve the progress of your kittens across certain game events:

  • Experience Retention: Normally, when a kitten dies or a reset occurs without certain upgrades, their accumulated experience and rank are lost. Immortalism allows kittens to retain their rank and XP even after they “die” from age or other factors (though they still need to be replaced by new kittens).
  • Leader Longevity: It is particularly useful for maintaining high-level Leaders. Since leaders provide bonuses based on their rank (like production boosts or price reductions), keeping those ranks intact is vital for efficiency.
  • Reduced Micromanagement: You won’t have to spend as much time re-assigning and re-leveling leaders in very long runs.

How to Unlock

To access Immortalism, you must have unlocked the Metaphysics tab (which requires the Astronomy and Philosophy technologies and at least one Ziggurat).

item.title: Sustainability vs Full Industrialisation
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Sustainability and Full Industrialization are mutually exclusive environmental policies. They are unlocked after researching Industrialization and require you to have previously chosen either the Strip Mining or Clear Cutting policy.

Sustainability

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Removes the happiness penalty (-2%) incurred from choosing Strip Mining or Clear Cutting.
    • Reduces global pollution by 5%.
  • Strategic Use: This policy is generally recommended for the first run. During your initial playthrough, you will likely only build one or two Factories to unlock the policy system, meaning you cannot take significant advantage of industrial boosts. Sustainability allows you to keep the production bonuses of your earlier policy (wood or minerals) while eliminating the morale hit.

Full Industrialization

  • Cost: 10,000 Culture.
  • Primary Effects:
    • Boosts Factory Power: Makes Factories 5% more powerful. This increases their base crafting bonus from 5% to 5.25% (or from 6% to 6.3% if Factory Logistics is researched).
    • Increases Pollution: Adds a +5% penalty to global pollution.
    • Space Production Synergy: Provides a 5% bonus to the “Space Production Bonus” generated by Factories once the Space Manufacturing upgrade is active.
  • Strategic Use: This is considered the superior choice for the mid-to-late game (typically starting from the second run onwards). Once you begin building dozens of Factories, the multiplicative nature of the crafting bonus becomes far more valuable than the small happiness gain from Sustainability.

Comparison Summary

Feature Sustainability Full Industrialization
Focus Happiness & Environment Crafting & Industrial Scaling
Happiness +2% (restores lost happiness) No bonus
Pollution -5% reduction +5% increase
Factories No effect +5% effectiveness boost
Space Bonus No effect +5% space production bonus
Best For First Run / Low Factory Count Mid-to-Late Game / High Factory Count

Strategic Recommendation: Most players choose Clear Cutting early in the run to resolve wood bottlenecks, then pivot to Full Industrialization once they have a robust factory network. In the late game, Full Industrialization is essential for the “Shatter Engine,” as it significantly scales Unobtainium production through Space Elevators and Orbital Arrays.

item.title: Knowledge sharing vs Cultural Exchange
item.description:
In Kittens Game, Knowledge Sharing and Cultural Exchange are mutually exclusive foreign policies unlocked after researching Astronomy and adopting the Diplomacy policy. Because they are in the same policy group, choosing one will permanently lock the other for the remainder of your current run.

Direct Comparison

Policy Cost Primary Effect Strategic Value
Knowledge Sharing 4,000 Culture +5% science income Generally considered suboptimal because science is relatively easy to generate through Scholars and astronomical events.
Cultural Exchange 4,000 Culture +5% culture income Generally preferred because culture is a notorious mid-game bottleneck required for manuscripts and advanced research.

Strategic Considerations

  • The Culture Bottleneck: Throughout the mid-game (the “Theology” era), players often struggle to produce enough culture to craft the manuscripts needed for scientific advancement. Sources explicitly recommend Cultural Exchange over Knowledge Sharing because “culture is slow” while “science is easy”.
  • Science Management: Science income is rarely the primary constraint on progress, as science caps (expanded by Libraries and Academies) are usually more significant hurdles than science production rates. Consequently, a 5% boost to science income often provides negligible benefits.
  • Iron Will Progression: In the specialised Iron Will mode (playing without kittens), where resources are even tighter, some guides suggest the Diplomacy → Cultural Exchange path as a way to bolster early culture production, which is vital for unlocking trade with the Nagas.

In summary, unless you are in a very specific scenario where your science production is lagging significantly behind your ability to store it, Cultural Exchange is the standard choice to help mitigate the game’s cultural bottlenecks.

Iron Will Bonuses

In Iron Will mode (where you have no kittens), these policies provide unique bonuses to your zebras and celestial events:

  • Clear Cutting: +10% bonus to catnip refinement (equivalent to one un-upgraded Lumber Mill).
  • Strip Mining: +10% bonus minerals from meteors.
  • Environmentalism: No specific Iron Will bonus is listed for the base policy, but it leads to Open Woodlands, which provides a 4.16% bonus to both refinement and meteor minerals.

Strategic Advice from the Sources

  • The Case for Clear Cutting: This is widely considered the strongest choice for early-to-mid-game runs. Wood is a major bottleneck when transitioning into the “Titanium Era,” as you need massive amounts of it for Observatories, Harbours, and Ships.
  • The Case for Strip Mining: Generally viewed as the least useful of the production-based choices. Minerals are typically easier to accumulate than wood through standard progression, making the 30% boost less impactful than the wood boost from Clear Cutting.
  • The Case for Environmentalism: Sources describe this policy as “pretty weak” because the 3% happiness boost is often outweighed by the raw production benefits of the other two. However, it is the only option that directly reduces pollution, which otherwise reduces catnip production and Solar Revolution bonuses.

Downstream Policy Unlocks

The choice you make here determines which advanced policies you can research later in the run after reaching Industrialization or Ecology:

Following Clear Cutting or Strip Mining:

  • Sustainability (10k Culture): Removes the -2% happiness penalty from your chosen production policy and provides a further -5% pollution reduction.
  • Full Industrialization (10k Culture): Makes Factories 5% more powerful (boosting their crafting bonus), but increases pollution by another +5%.

Following Environmentalism:

  • Conservation (10k Culture): Increases the happiness bonus from Environmentalism to +5% and provides another -5% pollution reduction.
  • Open Woodlands (10k Culture): A compromise policy that provides +12.5% wood and mineral production at the cost of +5% pollution.

In Kittens Game, Shark Relations refers to the trade mechanics and specialized policies associated with the Sharks, a neutral trade race discovered in the early-to-mid game. They are primarily used to acquire Catnip and cultural resources like Parchment and Manuscripts in exchange for Iron.

Trade Mechanics

Sharks are discovered around Year 20 (or Year 1 if you have the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade). Their attitude is Neutral, meaning they provide no baseline bonus or penalty to trade.

  • Primary Trade: You give 100 Iron; they give Catnip.
  • Secondary Gains: Successful trades have a chance to yield Parchment (25%), Manuscripts (15%), and Compendiums (10%).
  • Seasonal Bonus: They are most effective in Winter, providing a +45% bonus to catnip rewards.
  • Iron Will Strategy: In a “Black Sky” challenge, Sharks trade iron for Science instead of catnip.

Shark Relations Policies

Once you reach Shark Embassy Level 20 and possess the Diplomacy metaphysics upgrade, you can enact one of three mutually exclusive policies. Choosing one locks out the other two for that run.

Policy Effect Best Use Case
Scribes +25% Parchment chance, +15% Manuscript chance; +50% Iron cost per trade. Accelerating science when you have a massive surplus of Iron.
Merchants +3% Trade Ratio (scales up to +30% based on total trades completed). Long-term scaling of all trade rewards.
Botanists -75% Bio Lab energy, +1% Brewery catpower bonus, +25% Wood crafting bonus. Managing energy deficits or boosting late-game wood production.

Strategic Synergies

The Sharks are a core component of the “Winter Trade Loop,” which players use to bypass resource bottlenecks.

  1. The Loop: In Winter, trade Iron to the Sharks for massive amounts of Catnip. Refine that catnip into Wood, then trade the wood to the Griffins for Iron.
  2. Culture Grind: In challenges like Pacifism, where hunting for furs (to make parchment) is disabled, Sharks are the primary source of early cultural resources. Investing in Shark Embassies speeds up manuscript gains significantly.
  3. Pollution Mitigation: While not a direct trade benefit, the Lizard Relations: Ecologists policy reduces pollution, which helps preserve the high catnip production levels that the Sharks can supplement.

Hostility and Standing

While the Sharks are neutral, other races like the Griffins and Zebras are hostile. Using Tradeposts and the Caravanserai upgrade improves your standing with all races, but the Sharks’ neutral starting point makes them a reliable trade partner even before these upgrades are maxed out.

1. Cosmological Libertarianism (The “Meta” Choice)

This is widely considered the strongest option for most players.

  • Unobtainium is King: Unobtainium is the primary bottleneck for advanced space missions and time manipulation. A 15% boost to its production is significant because few other modifiers affect it directly.
  • Efficiency: Strategic guides recommend this over the others because “you REALLY need more unob” to progress through Phase 4 and establish a positive reset loop.

2. Order of the Stars (The Religious Choice)

This policy shifts your government’s focus to the heavens and the Order of the Sun.

3. Technocracy (The Niche Choice)

Technocracy provides a flat 20% increase to your Science storage capacity.

  • Redundancy: Strategy guides often label Technocracy as unnecessary because players have numerous other options to expand science storage—such as Compendiums, Observatories, and Data Centers—making a policy slot for science cap a lower priority.
  • Specific Utility: It is only truly beneficial if you are struggling to hit a specific, massive science threshold for a high-tier technology that other storage buildings cannot reach.

Choosing the Right Path

Because these Policy/ are mutually exclusive, selecting one will permanently lock the other two for the remainder of your current run.

  • For most runs: Choose Cosmological Libertarianism to speed up the acquisition of time crystals and eludium.
  • For deep-endgame/40k runs: You might consider Order of the Stars if your unobtainium production is already self-sustaining and you wish to focus purely on religious scaling.

Do you have a specific goal for your current run, such as farming Paragon or pushing for the 40k achievement? This could help determine which of these three would serve you best right now.

The overall strategy in the early game is to maximize global production through kittens and happiness, while overcoming specific resource bottlenecks like wood and manuscripts.

Here are the recommended policy choices during early game cycles, generally unlocked after researching Engineering:

1. Environment Policy/

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Clear Cutting Clear Cutting is highly recommended over its alternatives.
It provides a substantial +30% wood production bonus.
This boost is critical because wood becomes a “huge help” for constructing major mid-game buildings, such as observatories, harbours, and ships (required after researching Navigation).
Note: Although it introduces a small penalty of -2% happiness and +5% pollution, the resource gain outweighs these drawbacks during this developmental phase. The alternative, Environmentalism, is considered “pretty weak and doesn’t do much for you”.

2. Government Policy/ (Tier 1: Unlocked by Writing)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Tradition Tradition is generally preferred.
This policy accelerates the essential manuscript grind required to advance the science tree (especially toward Theology and Astronomy).
It reduces the manuscript cost ($-100$ culture and $-5$ parchment) and doubles the manuscript maximum culture effect.
Note: While Liberty increases the production effect of happiness, experts favour Tradition for accelerating the major cultural bottleneck. For early runs where unhappiness is a major factor, some players might consider Liberty to offset the production hit, but typically suggest switching to Tradition later.

3. Government Policy/ (Tier 2: Unlocked by Writing + Prior Policy)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Monarchy Monarchy is considered an “AMAZING” choice due to its flexibility and scaling potential.
It makes the leader’s trait twice as powerful. For example, a Leader with the Artisan trait will gain a +10% craft ratio instead of +5% (ignoring other bonuses).
This is powerful because a highly promoted leader can provide a massive boost to whatever resource is currently bottlenecking production, such as wood, science, or crafting efficiency.
Contrast: Alternatives like Republic and Autocracy offer small bonuses that are generally dwarfed by Monarchy’s multiplicative leader effect.

4. Philosophy Policy/ (Unlocked by Philosophy)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Epicureanism Epicureanism is often preferred because it focuses on boosting overall production.
Luxury resources (Furs, Ivory, Spice) will provide 11% happiness instead of the base 10%. Higher happiness is critical for increasing kitten productivity across all jobs.
By the time this policy is reached, trade and hunting systems should be robust enough to manage luxury consumption, making Stoicism (which halves consumption) less necessary.

5. Foreign Policy/ (Unlocked by Currency)

Policy Choice Rationale & Effect
Diplomacy Diplomacy is a standard early pick in the Foreign tree.
Each trade costs 5 less Catpower. Catpower is a foundational resource needed for hunting, exploration, and trade.
Furthermore, choosing Diplomacy leads to the subsequent policy Cultural Exchange, which boosts culture income.

In summary, for early game cycles, the optimal choices centre on Clear Cutting (for wood/infrastructure), Tradition (for manuscript/science velocity), and Monarchy/Epicureanism (for maximizing kitten production via happiness and leader efficiency).

Here is a comprehensive breakdown of the Frugality policy:

Overview and Prerequisite

  • Cost: Frugality costs 3500 Culture.
  • Prerequisite: The Frugality policy is unlocked only after first choosing Stoicism. Stoicism, in turn, is a policy in the Philosophy category, which requires researching Philosophy.
  • Context: Frugality is an option that appears as part of the philosophical policy tree, contrasted with Rationing.

Effects of Frugality

The Frugality policy focuses on optimizing output from economic buildings by reducing perceived corruption.

  • Effect: Stoic philosophers placed in charge of the mints make them more effective by reducing corruption. Consequently, Mints produce 10% more resources.

Strategic Considerations

Frugality is typically considered as an alternative choice when dealing with luxury resource consumption and happiness management:

  • Policy Path: Frugality follows the Stoicism path, which is centered on enduring hardship and reducing luxury consumption.
  • Alternative: Frugality is paired against the Rationing policy. Rationing, also following Stoicism, makes hunting more effective (+0.1 Hunting bonus) and reduces the catnip consumption increase per happiness by 10%.
  • Expert Opinion: Strategic advice suggests that Frugality might be chosen if consumption mitigation (provided by Stoicism or Rationing) is still insufficient, or if the increased output from Mints is desired, though one source notes, “…maybe the increased output from mints with Frugality… but probably not…”.

In essence, Frugality is a philosophical policy intended to boost the output of specialized financial/luxury-resource structures (Mints) after prioritizing austerity (Stoicism).

If consumption is outpacing a fully upgraded hunting team and tradepost effects, Stoicism, or its subsequent Policy/ like Rationing, may be necessary to control costs and maintain happiness levels.

In short, Epicureanism favours maximising output via happiness, while Stoicism favours optimising input via consumption reduction.

The choice between researching Machinery versus Steel in Kittens Game involves prioritizing different aspects of technological advancement and economic development during the mid-game phase, after researching Writing.

Machinery and Steel are considered “specialist Techs that won’t help you much right now” when Philosophy is the immediate priority to continue down the path of new science Techs like Theology. However, both are important for long-term growth.

Here is a comparison of the two technologies based on the sources:

Steel Technology

  • Cost and Prerequisite: Steel costs 12,000 Science and is unlocked by Writing.
  • Effect/Unlocks:
    • It enables the resource Steel, which is crafted from 100 Iron and 100 Coal.
    • It unlocks several key Workshop Upgrades, including:
      • Steel Axe (50% more effective Woodcutters).
      • Reinforced Warehouses (25% more storage for various resources).
      • Coal Furnace (Smelters produce 0.005 coal/tick while burning wood).
      • Deep Mining (Mines produce 0.003 coal/tick).
      • High Pressure Engine (reduces Steamworks coal consumption by 20%).
      • Steel Armour (Hunting bonus +0.5).
  • Strategic Importance: A general strategy suggests starting with Steel to get some useful upgrades that make your economy stronger. Acquiring Steel allows you to craft Steel, a composite part needed for Gears and complex machinery. You will need Steel later for construction, such as building Lumber Mills (which require Iron, and are needed to increase Wood output).

Machinery Technology

  • Cost and Prerequisite: Machinery costs 15,000 Science and is unlocked by Writing.
  • Effect/Unlocks:
    • It unlocks the Steamworks building.
    • It unlocks Workshop Upgrades, including:
      • Printing Press (Steamworks automatically prints manuscripts).
      • Workshop Automation (Steamworks converts small quantities of wood/minerals to beams/slabs annually if resource is near cap).
      • Crossbow (25% boost to catpower production from Hunters).
  • Strategic Importance: Machinery is valuable because it unlocks Steamworks. Steamworks consumes Coal to produce various handy items, including Manuscripts via the Printing Press upgrade. Acquiring Machinery allows for a way to automatically make manuscripts, and provides a hunting upgrade.

Strategic Takeaways

  1. Prioritization: It is suggested to research Steel first to boost economic efficiency via storage and production upgrades, then Machinery for automation and manuscript generation, before finally tackling Philosophy for Temples and Theology.
  2. Manufacturing: Steel is a necessary material for creating Gears. Gears, along with Steel and a Blueprint, are required to build a Steamworks, which is unlocked by Machinery.
  3. Manuscripts: While Philosophy leads to Theology (which requires Manuscripts), Steamworks (unlocked by Machinery) can automate manuscript production via the Printing Press upgrade.

In essence, Steel provides necessary structural components and early resource bonuses, while Machinery unlocks advanced automation and specialized buildings (Steamworks).

Diplomacy

Aspect Details

Prerequisite Currency
Effect Each trade costs 5 less catpower.
Policy Path Leads to Cultural Exchange or Knowledge Sharing (after researching Astronomy).
Strategic Value This policy is generally preferred because it unlocks the path to Cultural Exchange, which provides a bonus to Culture, a resource that is often slow to acquire.

Isolationism

Aspect Details

Prerequisite Currency

Strategic Recommendation

For most runs, Diplomacy is the recommended choice.

Space expansionism in Kittens Game refers to the phase where your civilisation leaves its home planet, Cath, to colonise the solar system. This era is officially unlocked by researching the Rocketry technology, which enables the Space tab and allows you to build rockets for interstellar missions.

Initial Unlocking and Missions

To begin your expansion, you must first navigate the “Titanium Era” to secure the necessary materials and storage caps. The first milestone is Orbital Launch, which requires a significant investment in Starcharts, Catpower, Science, and Oil.

Key initial missions include:

  • Orbital Launch: Unlocks the ability to deploy Satellites and build Space Elevators.
  • Moon Mission: The most critical early goal, as it provides access to Unobtainium through Lunar Outposts and significantly expanded storage via Moon Bases.
  • Dune Mission: Provides a source of Uranium (via Planet Crackers) and high-pressure Oil (via Hydraulic Fracturers).
  • Piscine Mission: Unlocks Research Vessels, which are essential for generating large quantities of Starcharts in the mid-to-late game.

Critical Resources for Space

Successful space expansion relies on several specific resources that become the primary bottlenecks of the late game:

  • Starcharts: Found by observing astronomical events or produced by Satellites and Research Vessels; these are the “currency” of space travel.
  • Unobtainium (UO): A rare resource refined from Uranium at Lunar Outposts. It is the gateway to Time Crystals, Eludium, and the endgame storage loops.
  • Oil and Kerosene: Oil is used for initial launches, while advanced missions require Kerosene, a fuel processed from oil.
  • Antimatter: Produced by Sunlifters (Helios), it is used for high-tier upgrades and increasing resource caps.

Strategic Optimization

Space expansion is not just about exploring; it is a mechanism for scaling your civilisation’s resource caps geometrically.

  • Space Manufacturing: This is a vital workshop upgrade that allows your Factories to improve the production of space buildings. Without this, space structures often provide marginal returns.
  • Global Multipliers: Buildings like the Space Elevator (reduces oil costs) and Orbital Array (provides a 2% bonus to all space structures) are essential for making expansion efficient.
  • Storage Caps: Late-game progression is gated by the 8.14 billion Unobtainium storage requirement needed for 100 Chronospheres. This is achieved through massive investment in Moon Bases, Cryostations, and AI Bases.

Technocracy is only truly useful if you are attempting to reach a specific, massive science threshold for an endgame technology (like Blackchain or Exophysics) and have already maxed out all other science storage options without reaching the required amount.

  • The Titanium Bottleneck: Since Zebras are the primary source of Titanium, making them more hostile and reducing their trade yield is generally counter-productive.
  • Hostility Mitigation: Expert advice suggests that Appeasement is the only real option until you have enough Tradeposts (typically 85, or 58 with Diplomacy) to negate Zebra hostility naturally.
  • Late Game Viability: Bellicosity only becomes viable once Zebra hostility has been completely negated through infrastructure, and you wish to marginally boost trades with friendly races like the Lizards or Sharks.

The choice between the Liberty and Tradition Policy/ in Kittens Game represents an early decision regarding how your civilization addresses population growth, resource management, and scientific advancement. Both Policy/ become available once you have researched Writing and both cost 150 Culture.

This choice is particularly important because once one is selected, the other is locked out, and this initial decision influences the subsequent Government Policy/ you can pursue.

Here is a comparison of their purpose, effects, and strategic recommendations:

1. Tradition Policy

Purpose and Effects:

  • Manuscript Efficiency: Tradition is described as being “Good for small culture oriented societies”. Its primary effect is reducing the cost and increasing the impact of Manuscripts.
    • Cost Reduction: Manuscript cost is reduced by 100 Culture and 5 Parchment.
    • Culture Cap Boost: It doubles the manuscript max culture effect.
  • Expert Recommendation: “Monstrous Advice” strongly recommends Tradition (“all the way!”) because manuscripts are crucial for progression, and making them cheaper and more effective is highly beneficial.

Progression Path:

  • Choosing Tradition allows you to later select Monarchy or Autocracy (both costing 1500 Culture).

2. Liberty Policy

Purpose and Effects:

  • Happiness Focus: Liberty is intended for societies focused on happiness, addressing the natural unhappiness that arises from increasing population.
    • Happiness Bonus: It increases the production effect of happiness by 10%.
    • Population Bonus: It adds free housing for one kitten.
  • Contextual Use: In early runs, the Liberty policy can be obtained to offset a “big production hit due to happiness”.

Strategic Critique:

  • “Monstrous Advice” labels Liberty as a “noob trap” because it promises to solve a problem (low happiness/production) that can often be managed through other means, such as accumulating Karma from resets or building Amphitheatres.
  • The “Kittensgame starter guide,” however, suggests that in early runs, if progression is slowing due to low happiness/high population penalty, obtaining Liberty can be useful to mitigate that production hit. However, in later runs (once Karma is acquired), switching to Tradition may be preferable.

Progression Path:

  • Choosing Liberty allows you to later select Republic or Autocracy (both costing 1500 Culture).

Summary of Differences

Policy Primary Benefit Recommended Strategy Subsequent Governments
Tradition Reduces the cost of manuscripts and increases their culture effect. Highly recommended by experts for improving long-term progress and managing the manuscript bottleneck. Monarchy, Autocracy.
Liberty Increases kitten production based on Happiness and provides one free housing unit. Useful in specific early runs if happiness penalties are severely impacting production. Republic, Autocracy.

In essence, Tradition invests in the efficiency of your scientific engine (Manuscript production), while Liberty attempts to mask the symptoms of low kitten Happiness to maintain production. For most players seeking rapid progress, the permanent resource efficiency gained from Tradition is favored, as manuscripts quickly become a bottleneck required for advanced technologies like Theology and Astronomy.
